outputs.explanation: This is a scatter plot in which each of the 141 plotted markers represents one individual sample's rhythmicity index and period; the marginal histograms show the count distribution of these same individual measurements. Since the points themselves are the individual data, no additional overlay is required.

Each marker plotted here is not an individual measurement but the mean ± s.d. of 6 replicate samples per reporter (n=2 biological replicates x technical triplicates/duplicates, as stated in the caption). Because the points represent averaged/aggregated values rather than raw individual samples, this functions like an error-bar/bar-chart summary and the underlying individual replicate values are not shown anywhere in the panel.

This panel shows fitted normal-distribution density curves per subtype (a line/curve-type plot). Overlaying individual points on such continuous density curves is not meaningful and would make them unreadable, so this plot type is exempt from the individual-points requirement.

This is a box plot showing quartiles, median, and outliers of ridge lengths; box plots already convey the data distribution and are exempt from the requirement to overlay individual points (notably, individual sample points are in fact also plotted here, though this is not required for the check to pass).

These are polar histograms showing the probability distribution of Bmal1-Per2 phase differences; as with standard histograms, the bar heights themselves convey the distribution of the underlying data, so a separate overlay of individual points is not required.

This is a polar histogram summarizing phase-difference distributions averaged by subtype; like other histogram-type plots, the bar shape itself conveys distributional information and does not require an additional overlay of individual points.

This panel is a line plot showing one example raw signal trace with its fitted decaying sinusoid and decay envelope; it illustrates a single example rather than an average across samples, so the individual-data-point requirement does not apply.

Each of the 117 plotted markers represents one individual sample's fitted amplitude and decay rate; the error bars reflect the statistical uncertainty of the curve fit for that single sample (not variability across replicates being averaged), so the points already constitute the individual data and no further overlay is needed.
